summary.headline: GCPL Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 19% YoY (15% constant currency) on 8% underlying volume growth; net profit up 14% to INR523 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY (15% in constant currency) with 8% underlying volume growth, EBITDA grew 12% and net profit rose 14% to INR523 crore. Standalone sales grew 13% on 7% underlying volume growth, after an estimated 150 bps hit from trade inventory correction, which also mildly hit standalone EBITDA. GUAM (Africa) and Indonesia were the strongest international contributors, while input inflation was among the highest in many years and was offset by pricing, cost savings and A&P optimisation. Management held FY27 guidance of high single-digit standalone UVG and double-digit consolidated revenue and EBITDA growth, and said revenues are running ahead of plan.

financial_highlights.change: Second consecutive quarter of high-teens growth
Management targets double-digit consolidated EBITDA growth in FY27
Underlying volume growth 7%; ~150 bps impact from trade inventory correction
Led by air fresheners and home care liquids

segments.name: Home Care (India)
segments.commentary: Value growth of 19%, led by air fresheners and home care liquids; market share gained in household insecticides (HI). Electric portfolio improved sequentially with the 6 minutes campaign; Godrej Fab grew at a strong double-digit rate.

segments.name: Personal Care (India)
segments.commentary: Value growth of 8%, with soaps stable despite significant price increases and grammage reduction against a favourable comparator. Premium liquids, Cinthol body wash, hair colour (share gains) and perfumes/deodorants (strong double-digit growth) contributed; volume growth lagged value growth.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Sales +20% with 8% underlying volume growth and EBITDA +12%, aided by El Nino-driven mosquito infestation tailwind; LPG prices doubled. Newer portfolio (LV, Pocket) sustained double-digit underlying volume growth.

segments.name: GUAM (Africa)
segments.commentary: Sales +40% INR (+23% constant currency), 16% underlying volume growth, EBITDA +43%; seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit top-line growth and eleventh of double-digit bottom-line growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance held: high single-digit underlying volume growth in standalone and double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth at consolidated level; revenues running ahead of plan in H1, with confidence to exceed in certain areas.
Commodity inflation expected to be slightly higher in Q3 than Q2; company will price for profit growth rather than margin, focusing on consolidated EBITDA YoY growth.
Further calibrated pricing planned in soaps and liquid detergents, where margins remain below normative levels.
Management expects to hold double-digit consolidated EBITDA growth; India EBITDA shape expected to broadly continue with some up-and-down quarters.
International business expected to deliver double-digit volume growth; Indonesia growth at higher levels still to be proven.
Capacity expansions for GUAM businesses at high utilisation due in the next few months.
capex_capacity: GUAM existing businesses running at very high capacity utilisation, constraining growth; capacity expansions due in the next few months.
Godrej Spic (toilet cleaner) scaled nationally after Tamil Nadu success; significant distribution headroom remains.
Trade inventory being reduced to system-defined levels to support primary sales run without manual intervention.
demand_pricing: Input costs: one of the highest inflationary impacts in many years, driven by crude derivatives, palm oil and commodities; impact approximately high single digit in India and Indonesia.
Pricing actions taken across portfolio, large cost-savings programme, and media/trade spend optimisation used to offset inflation; share of voice to be kept range-bound.
Soaps category seeing trade inventory correction, price-volume recalibration and grammage cuts; detergents growth described as strong, with powder-to-liquid shift and formalisation benefit.

Media spend in India standalone declined for seven consecutive quarters (per analyst: -7% in Q1, -17% in Q2); management attributes it equally to category spend reduction in soaps/detergents and to better-reach, lower-cost media buying in the rest of the portfolio.
New launches: Godrej Rizz (selected West and South India markets), Godrej Zap stain remover online, GUAM HI incense sticks; Ezee entering season with early traction.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in digital advertising capability, daily sales hustle, and HI communication since the management transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital and influencer capabilities are being built and it expects top-percentile digital positioning within a few quarters, not tied to spend percentage. Operational excellence focus is being reset via trade inventory correction. New HI ad features the RNF product and is designed to be clutter-breaking.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and skill-set for the India CEO hire, and progress on pet care and new bathroom cleaner?
qa_highlights.answer: India CEO search is in a robust process, prioritising Godrej values and entrepreneurial mindset over speed. Godrej Spic is now national. Pet care is still in learning phase; management will give milestones next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Personal Care volume growth well below 8% value growth, and which parts are weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Soaps saw trade inventory correction (large SKUs typically build inventory) and price-volume recalibration after steep price increases; margins still below normative. Hair colour gained share strongly. Detergents growth is in line with trend.

qa_highlights.question: How should Q3/Q4 India margins and EBITDA be viewed given commodity lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity inflation expected slightly higher in Q3 vs Q2. Company will focus on consolidated EBITDA YoY growth rather than margin, aiming to hold double-digit consolidated EBITDA growth; India may see some up-and-down quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are H2 volume risks from inflation or season in detergents and HI?
qa_highlights.answer: Detergents not impacted by inflation on volume; HI season looks fine as El Nino impact was mainly in H1. Management expects to sustain volume trend lines.

qa_highlights.question: Is the decline in India standalone A&P spend structural or cyclical?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: soaps and detergents category spend has fallen and the company is balancing spend to keep share of voice at target, while the rest of the portfolio gets higher reach at lower cost via media agency practices. Management gave roughly equal weight to the two factors.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are Indonesia and GUAM growth beyond this year, and what is GUAM's mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Indonesia: a few bps of this year's growth is attributed to better weather; management is building more growth flywheels and expects double-digit international volume growth. GUAM: growth is broad-based, from core hair and new categories like Mega Growth Mousse and Darling styling products; hair colour has grown double digit in volume for 7-8 quarters. No split of core vs new given.

risks_watch: Trade inventory correction in soaps and large SKUs may continue to weigh on standalone sales and EBITDA.
Commodity inflation expected to be higher in Q3 than Q2; pricing actions need to offset without hurting volumes, especially in soaps.
Indonesia's growth benefited from El Nino-driven weather; management acknowledged this is partly seasonal.
India CEO appointment still pending; management transition and team changes (digital, operational excellence) are still being put in place.
A&P spend in India standalone has declined for seven consecutive quarters; watch share of voice and brand investment.
Pet care business still in pilot with no milestones disclosed until next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline numbers and guidance, but cautious on the India soaps and margin outlook and evasive on specifics for the new India CEO and pet care. Management repeatedly framed changes as structural and in progress rather than quantified.
key_quotes: We continue to hold our FY27 guidance, high single-digit underlying volume growth in stand-alone and double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth at a consol level.
it's important to kind of price for profit growth rather than to price for margin.
GUAM has now delivered 7 consecutive quarters of double-digit top line growth and 11 consecutive quarters of double-digit bottom line growth.

adds.what: GUAM businesses capacity expansions (size not quantified)

growth.why: FY27 guidance held at high single-digit standalone volume growth and double-digit consolidated revenue and EBITDA growth; H1 revenue running ahead of plan, backed by pricing, GUAM capacity expansions due in the next few months (size unquantified) and share gains, though no specific capacity numbers were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Commodity inflation is high single digit in India and Indonesia and is expected to be slightly higher in Q3 than Q2, and management will price for profit growth rather than margin, so margin expansion is not the stated aim.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: GUAM businesses run at very high utilisation and capacity expansions are due in the next few months, though size is not quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 guidance held at high single-digit standalone UVG (Q2 was 7%) and double-digit international volume growth, with GUAM volume at 16% and Indonesia at 8%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Very high utilisation in GUAM is noted, but no new capex amount or plant has been announced; the expansion already underway may be the only capacity move.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenues are running ahead of plan in H1 and management has confidence to exceed in certain areas, yet guidance was only held, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Trade inventory correction cost about 150 bps of standalone sales growth, soaps margins are still below normative, and Q3 commodity inflation is higher than Q2, though consolidated double-digit EBITDA growth is still targeted.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Godrej Rizz is rolling out in selected West and South markets, Zap stain remover is going online, GUAM HI incense sticks are coming, and Ezee is entering season; pet care milestones are due next quarter.

rows.label: Pricing and cost savings offset input inflation
rows.why: Input inflation is high single digit in India and Indonesia; pricing, a large cost-savings programme and media optimisation were used to offset it in Q2, with further calibrated soap and liquid detergent pricing planned.

rows.label: Trade inventory correction ends
rows.why: Trade inventory is being reduced to system-defined levels, which cost about 150 bps of standalone sales growth in Q2 and will keep weighing on soaps sales until the correction is done.

rows.label: India CEO hire and digital capability build
rows.why: India CEO search is in a robust process with no timeline, and digital and influencer capabilities are being built with top-percentile positioning expected within a few quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on headline growth, guidance and GUAM/Indonesia momentum but cautious on India soaps, margins and inflation, and evasive on the India CEO and pet care timing; analysts pressed on Personal Care volume lagging value, and on whether the cut in A&P spend is structural or cyclica
